verses.text: 1:1After Saul died, David returned from striking Amalek. David stayed in Ziklag for two days.
1:2On the third day, behold, a man came from the camp, from Saul’s people, with his garments torn and earth on his head. When he came in to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down to him.
1:3David said to him, “Where have you come from?” He said to him, “I have come safely away from Israel’s camp.”
1:4David said to him, “What is this report? Tell me.” He said, “The people fled from the war, and many of the people have fallen and died. Saul also died, and Jonathan his son died.”
1:5David said to the young man reporting to him, “How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son have died?”
1:6The young man reporting to him said, “By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa. Behold, Saul was leaning on his spear, and behold, the chariots and cavalry commanders had closed in on him.
1:7He looked behind him and saw me. He called me, and I said, ‘Here I am.’
1:8He said to me, ‘Who are you?’ I said, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
1:9He said to me, ‘Stand over me now and put me to death, for terrible darkness has seized me, for my whole soul is in me.’
1:10I stood over him and put him to death, for I knew he would not live after he had fallen. I took the royal crown on his head and the armlet on his arm, and have brought them here to my lord.”
1:11David took hold of his garments and tore them, and all the men with him tore their garments.
1:12They mourned, wept, and fasted until evening for Saul, for Jonathan his son, for Judah’s people, and for the house of Israel, because they had been struck by the sword.
1:13David said to the young man reporting to him, “Where are you from?” He said, “I am the son of an Amalekite resident alien.”
1:14David said to him, “How were you not afraid to bring your hand against the Lord’s anointed to destroy him?”
1:15David called one of his young men and said, “Come near and strike him.” He struck him, and he died.
1:16David said to him, “Your blood is on your own head, for your mouth answered against you, saying, ‘I put the Lord’s anointed to death.’”
1:17David lamented this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son,
1:18and he gave orders to teach the sons of Judah—behold, it is written in the Book of the Upright—
1:19“Set up a memorial, Israel, for the dead, slain upon your heights! How the mighty have fallen!
1:20Do not report it in Gath, and do not proclaim good news in Ashkelon’s exits, lest the daughters of the foreigners rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

1:21Mountains in Gilboa, let no dew descend and no rain upon you, nor fields of firstfruits! For there the shield of the mighty was treated with contempt;
Saul’s shield was not anointed with oil.
1:22From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, Jonathan’s bow did not turn back empty, and Saul’s sword did not return empty.
1:23Saul and Jonathan, loved and beautiful, not separated, splendid in their life and not separated in their death: swifter than eagles, they proved stronger than lions.
1:24Daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with your adornment, who put gold adornment upon your clothing.
1:25How the mighty have fallen in the midst of war! Jonathan lies slain upon your heights.
1:27How the mighty have fallen, and the equipment of war has perished!”
2:1After this, David inquired of the Lord, saying, “Shall I go up into one of Judah’s cities?” The Lord said to him, “Go up.” David said, “Where shall I go up?” He said, “To Hebron.”
2:2David went up there to Hebron, and both his wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail, the wife of Nabal the Carmelite,
2:3and the men with him, each man and his household; and they settled in Hebron’s cities.
2:4Men of Judea came and anointed David there to reign over the house of Judah. They reported to David, “The men of Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”

2:5David sent messengers to the leaders of Jabesh in Gilead and said to them, “Blessed are you by the Lord, because you have shown this mercy to your lord, to Saul, the Lord’s anointed, and buried him and Jonathan his son.
2:6Now may the Lord show you mercy and truth. Indeed, I too will do these good things for you, because you have done this thing.
2:7Now let your hands be strong, and become men of valour, for your lord Saul has died. Indeed, the house of Judah has anointed me king over themselves.”
2:8Abner son of Ner, Saul’s commander in chief, took Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him up from the camp to Mahanaim.
2:9He made him king over the land of Gilead, over Thasiri, over Jezreel, over Ephraim, over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
2:10Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years, except over the house of Judah, who followed David.
2:11The time David reigned in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
2:12Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

2:13Joab son of Zeruiah and David’s servants went out from Hebron and met them together at Gibeon’s spring. They sat down, one group on this side of Gibeon’s spring and the other on that side of the spring.
2:14Abner said to Joab, “Let the young men rise now and play before us.” Joab said, “Let them rise.”
2:15They rose and passed over by number: twelve of Benjamin’s young men belonging to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve of David’s servants.
2:16Each seized his opponent’s head with his hand and thrust his sword into his opponent’s side, and they fell together. That place was named Portion of the Plotters, which is in Gibeon.
2:17The battle was very severe that day, and Abner and Israel’s men were defeated before David’s servants.
2:18The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel was light on his feet, like a gazelle in the field.
2:19Asahel pursued Abner and did not turn to the right or to the left from following Abner.
2:20Abner looked behind him and said, “Are you Asahel?” He said, “It is I.”
2:21Abner said to him, “Turn to the right or to the left. Seize one of the young men and take his full armour for yourself.” But Asahel was unwilling to turn aside from following him.
2:22Abner again said to Asahel, “Withdraw from me, lest I strike you to the ground. How could I lift my face to Joab? And where do these things lead? Return to your brother Joab.”

2:23He was unwilling to withdraw. Abner struck him in the loins with the butt of the spear, and the spear passed out through his back. He fell there and died beneath him. Everyone who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stopped.
2:24Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. The sun was setting when they reached the hill of Amman, facing Gai, on Gibeon’s desert road.
2:25The sons of Benjamin gathered behind Abner and formed one company. They stood on the top of a hill.
2:26Abner called to Joab and said, “Will the sword devour for ever? Do you not know it will be bitter in the end? How long will you fail to tell the people to turn back from pursuing our brothers?”
2:27Joab said, “As the Lord lives, if you had not spoken, then from early morning the people would have gone up, each after his brother.”
2:28Joab sounded the trumpet, and all the people withdrew. They did not pursue Israel and did not continue fighting.
2:29Abner and his men went westward all that night. They crossed the Jordan, traveled the entire stretch, and came to the camp.
2:30Joab returned from following Abner and gathered all the people. Nineteen men of David’s servants, and Asahel, were counted.
2:31David’s servants struck down three hundred sixty men from the sons of Benjamin, Abner’s men, belonging to him.
2:32They carried Asahel away and buried him in his father’s tomb at Bethlehem. Joab and the men with him traveled all night, and day dawned for them in Hebron.
3:1The war between Saul’s house and David’s house lasted a long time. David’s house grew stronger and stronger, while Saul’s house grew weaker and weaker.
3:2Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite;
3:3his second was Daluia, by Abigail the Carmelite; and the third was Absalom son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
3:4the fourth was Ornia son of Phengith; and the fifth was Sabatia, by Abital;
3:5and the sixth was Ithream, by Eglah, David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
3:6While there was war between Saul’s house and David’s house, Abner was holding power over Saul’s house.
3:7Saul had a concubine, Rizpah daughter of Ial. Mephibosheth son of Saul said to Abner, “Why have you gone in to my father’s concubine?”

3:8Abner became very angry over Mephibosheth’s statement. Abner said to him, “Am I a dog’s head? Today I have shown mercy to the house of Saul your father, and toward brothers and acquaintances, and I have not deserted to David’s house. Yet today you call me to account for wrongdoing concerning a woman!
3:9May God do these things to Abner, and add these things to him, for just as the Lord swore to David, so I will do for him this very day:
3:10to remove the kingdom from Saul’s house and raise up David’s throne over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”
3:11Mephibosheth could no longer answer Abner a word, because he feared him.
3:12Abner sent messengers to David at Thailam, where he was at the time, saying, “Make your covenant with me, and behold, my hand will be with you to turn all the house of Israel to you.”
3:13David said, “I will gladly make a covenant with you. But I ask one thing of you: you will not see my face unless you bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see my face.”
3:14David sent messengers to Mephibosheth son of Saul, saying, “Give me back my wife Michal, whom I obtained for a hundred foreskins of foreigners.”
3:15Mephibosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel son of Selles.
3:16Her husband went with her, weeping behind her as far as Barakim. Abner said to him, “Return.” He went back.
3:17Abner said to Israel’s elders, “In days past you were seeking David to reign over you.
3:18Now act, for the Lord spoke concerning David, saying, ‘By the hand of My servant David I will save Israel from the hand of foreigners and from the hand of all their enemies.’”
3:19Abner spoke in Benjamin’s hearing. Abner went to speak in David’s hearing at Hebron about everything that pleased Israel and the whole house of Benjamin.
3:20Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men. David made a drinking feast for Abner and the men with him.

3:21Abner said to David, “I will rise now and go and gather all Israel to my lord the king. I will make a covenant with you, and you will reign over all that your soul desires.” David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.
3:22Behold, David’s servants and Joab were arriving from an expedition, bringing much spoil with them. Abner was not with David in Hebron, for David had sent him away and he had departed in peace.
3:23Joab and all his army were brought in. Joab was told, “Abner son of Ner has come to David, and he has sent him away, and he departed in peace.”
3:24Joab came in to the king and said, “What is this you have done? Behold, Abner came to you! Why have you sent him away, and he has departed in peace?
3:25Do you not know the wickedness of Abner son of Ner? He came to deceive you, to learn your going out and your coming in, and to learn everything you are doing.”
3:26Joab returned from David and sent messengers after Abner. They brought him back from the well of Seiram, but David did not know.
3:27Abner returned to Hebron. Joab took him aside beside the gate to speak with him while lying in wait, and struck him there in the loins. He died for the blood of Asahel, Joab’s brother.
3:28Afterward David heard and said, “I and my kingdom are for ever guiltless before the Lord of the blood of Abner son of Ner.

3:29Let it fall upon Joab’s head and upon his father’s whole house. May Joab’s house never lack someone with a seminal discharge, someone who is leprous, someone holding a staff, someone falling by the sword, or someone lacking bread.”
3:30Joab and Abishai his brother kept watch for Abner because he had put their brother Asahel to death in the battle at Gibeon.
3:31David said to Joab and all the people with him, “Tear your garments, put on sackcloth, and beat yourselves in mourning before Abner.” King David walked behind the bier.
3:32They buried Abner in Hebron. The king lifted his voice and wept at his grave, and all the people wept over Abner.
3:33The king lamented over Abner and said, “Should Abner die according to Nabal’s death?
3:34Your hands were not bound; your feet were not in fetters. He did not bring near, as Nabal; before men of injustice you fell.” All the people gathered to weep over him.

3:35All the people came to have David eat a funeral meal with bread while it was still day. David swore, “May God do these things to me, and add these things: unless the sun sets, I will certainly not taste bread or anything at all.”
3:36All the people understood, and everything the king did before the people pleased them.
3:37All the people and all Israel knew that day that putting Abner son of Ner to death had not come from the king.
3:38The king said to his servants, “Do you not know that a great leader has fallen this day in Israel,
3:39and that today I am a kinsman and one appointed by a king? But these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are harder than I. May the Lord repay the evildoer according to his wickedness.”
4:1When Mephibosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands grew weak, and all Israel’s men lost heart.

4:2Mephibosheth son of Saul had two men who led bands. One was named Baanah, and the second Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, from the sons of Benjamin, for Beeroth was counted as belonging to Benjamin’s sons.
4:3The Beerothites had escaped to Gittaim and remained there as resident aliens to this day.

4:4Jonathan son of Saul had a son whose feet had been injured. He was five years old when news of Saul and Jonathan his son came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled. As she hurried and withdrew, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
4:5The sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went and entered Mephibosheth’s house in the heat of the day. He was sleeping in bed at midday.
4:6Behold, the woman keeping the house’s door was cleaning wheat. She became drowsy and fell asleep, and the brothers Rechab and Baanah slipped past unnoticed.
4:7They entered the house while Mephibosheth was sleeping on his bed in his bedchamber. They struck him, killed him, and removed his head. They took his head and went by the westward road all night.

4:8They brought Mephibosheth’s head to David at Hebron and said to the king, “Behold, the head of Mephibosheth son of Saul your enemy, who sought your life! The Lord has given the lord king vengeance upon his enemies, as on this day, upon Saul your enemy and his offspring.”
4:9David answered Rechab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, “As the Lord lives, who redeemed my life from every distress,
4:10the one who reported to me that Saul had died was like a bearer of good news before me, and I seized him and killed him in Ziklag—the one to whom I was supposed to give a reward for good news!
4:11And now wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house, on his bed! Now I will require his blood from your hands and destroy you from the earth.”
4:12David commanded his young men, and they killed them, cut off their hands and feet, and hung them beside the spring in Hebron. They buried Mephibosheth’s head in the tomb of Abner son of Ner.
5:1All Israel’s tribes came to David at Hebron and said to him, “Behold, we are your bones and your flesh.
5:2In days past, when Saul was king over us, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them in. The Lord said to you, ‘You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over Israel.’”
5:3All Israel’s elders came to the king at Hebron. King David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the Lord, and they anointed David king over all Israel.
5:4David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years,
5:5seven years and six months he reigned in Hebron over Judah, and thirty-three years he reigned over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.

5:6David and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites inhabiting the land. David was told, “You will not come in here,” for the blind and the lame resisted, saying, “David will not come in here.”
5:7David captured the stronghold of Zion, which is the city of David.

5:8David said that day, “Everyone striking a Jebusite, let him attack with a dagger both the lame and the blind and those who hate David’s soul.” Therefore they will say, “The blind and the lame shall not enter the Lord’s house.”
5:9David settled in the stronghold, and it was called the city of David. He built the city around from the citadel, and his own house.
5:10David grew greater and greater, and the Lord Almighty was with him.
5:11Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, cedar wood, woodworkers, and stoneworkers. They built a house for David.
5:12David knew that the Lord had prepared him as king over Israel and that his kingdom had been exalted for the sake of his people Israel.
5:13David took more wives and concubines from Jerusalem after coming from Hebron, and David had more sons and daughters.
5:14These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon;
5:15Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, and Japhia;
5:16Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet;
5:16aSamae, Iessibath, Nathan, Galamaan, Iebaar, Theesous, Elphalat, Naged, Naphek, Ianatha, Leasamys, Baalimath, Eliphalath.
5:17The foreigners heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, and all the foreigners went up to seek David. David heard and went down to the stronghold.
5:18The foreigners arrived and gathered in the Valley of the Titans.

5:19David inquired through the Lord, saying, “Shall I go up against the foreigners? Wilt Thou deliver them into my hands?” The Lord said to David, “Go up, for I will certainly deliver the foreigners into your hands.”

5:20David came from the Upper Breaches and struck the foreigners there. David said, “The Lord has broken through my enemies, the foreigners, before me as waters break through.” Therefore that place was named Upper Breaches.
5:21They abandoned their gods there, and David and the men with him took them.
5:22The foreigners came up again and gathered in the Valley of the Titans.
5:23David inquired through the Lord, and the Lord said, “Do not go up to meet them. Turn away from them, and you will come upon them near the place of weeping.
5:24When you hear the sound of the closing together of the grove of weeping, then go down against them, for then the Lord will go out before you to strike in the battle with the foreigners.”
5:25David did as the Lord commanded him and struck the foreigners from Gibeon as far as the land of Gezer.
6:1David again gathered all the young men from Israel, about seventy thousand.

6:2David and all the people with him rose and went from Judah’s rulers on an ascent to bring up from there the ark of God, over which is called the name of the Lord of hosts, enthroned upon the cherubim above it.
6:3He placed the ark of the Lord on a new cart and brought it from Abinadab’s house on the hill. Uzzah and his brothers, Abinadab’s sons, were driving the cart
6:4with the ark, and his brothers were walking before the ark.
6:5David and the sons of Israel were celebrating before the Lord on tuned instruments, with strength and songs, with lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals, and pipes.
6:6They came to Nodab’s threshing floor. Uzzah stretched out his hand toward the ark of God to hold it fast, and gripped it because the bull calf had pulled it aside, so as to hold it fast.
6:7The Lord became angry with Uzzah, and God struck him there. He died there beside the ark of the Lord, before God.
6:8David became disheartened because the Lord had made a breach against Uzzah. That place was called Breach of Uzzah to this day.
6:9David feared the Lord that day, saying, “How can the ark of the Lord come to me?”
6:10David was unwilling to turn the ark of the Lord’s covenant aside to himself in the city of David. David turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
6:11The ark of the Lord remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months. The Lord blessed Obed-edom’s whole household and all that was his.

6:12King David was told, “The Lord has blessed Obed-edom’s household and all that is his because of the ark of God.” David went and brought the ark of the Lord up from Obed-edom’s house to the city of David with gladness.
6:13With them were seven dancing companies carrying the ark, and a calf and a lamb as a sacrifice.
6:14David was playing on tuned instruments before the Lord, and David was clothed in a distinctive robe.
6:15David and the whole house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting and the sound of a trumpet.
6:16As the ark reached the city of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked through the window. She saw King David dancing and playing before the Lord, and despised him in her heart.
6:17They brought the ark of the Lord in and set it in its place, inside the tent David had pitched for it. David offered whole burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord.
6:18When David finished offering the whole burnt offerings and peace offerings together, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts.

6:19He distributed to all the people, the whole force of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, both men and women, to each a loaf of bread, a hearth cake, and a flat cake from a frying pan. Then all the people went away, each to his own house.

6:20David returned to bless his household. Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet David, blessed him, and said, “How glorious Israel’s king has been today, uncovering himself today before the eyes of his servants’ servant women, as one of the dancers openly uncovers himself!”

6:21David said to Michal, “I will dance before the Lord. Blessed is the Lord, who chose me above your father and above his whole house to appoint me ruler over His people, over Israel. I will celebrate and dance before the Lord,
6:22and I will uncover myself still in this way and be worthless in your eyes, and with the servant women among whom you said I was to be honoured.”
6:23Michal daughter of Saul had no child until the day of her death.
7:1When the king was settled in his house and the Lord had given him possession on every side, away from all his surrounding enemies,
7:2the king said to Nathan the prophet, “Look now, I dwell in a cedar house, while the ark of God remains inside the tent.”
7:3Nathan said to the king, “Go and do all that is in your heart, for the Lord is with you.”
7:4That night a word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
7:5“Go and say to My servant David, ‘Thus says the Lord: You will not build Me a house for Me to dwell in,
7:6for I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the sons of Israel up from Egypt until this day. I have been moving about in a lodging and a tent.
7:7Wherever I passed through among all Israel, did I ever speak to one of Israel’s tribes whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, “Why have you not built Me a cedar house?”
7:8Now say this to My servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold to be ruler over My people, over Israel,
7:9and I was with you wherever you went and destroyed all your enemies before you, and I made you renowned, according to the name of the great ones on the earth.
7:10I will appoint a place for My people Israel and plant them there. They will dwell on their own and worry no more. No unjust man will again humble them as at the beginning,
7:11from the days when I appointed judges over My people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies, and the Lord will announce to you that you will build Him a house.
7:12When your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who will be from your own body, and prepare his kingdom.
7:13He will build Me a house for My name, and I will set his throne upright for ever.
7:14I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to Me. If his wrongdoing comes, I will correct him with the rod of men and the afflictions of human beings.
7:15But I will not withdraw My mercy from him as I withdrew it from those whom I removed from before Me.
7:16His house and his kingdom will be made sure for ever before Me, and his throne will be set upright for ever.’”
7:17Nathan spoke to David according to all these words and all this vision.
7:18King David went in and sat before the Lord. He said, “Who am I, my Lord, Lord, and what is my house, that Thou hast loved me to this extent?
7:19Yet it was reckoned a small thing before Thee, my Lord, Lord, and Thou hast spoken of Thy servant’s house far into the future. This is the law of the human being, my Lord, Lord.
7:20What more can David say to Thee? Now Thou knowest Thy servant, my Lord, Lord.
7:21Because of Thy word Thou hast acted, and according to Thy heart Thou hast done all this greatness, to make it known to Thy servant,
7:22so that Thou mayest be magnified, my Lord, Lord, for there is none like Thee and no God besides Thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

7:23What other nation on earth is like Thy people Israel? God led them to redeem a people for Himself, for Thee to make Thyself a name, to bring about greatness and a manifestation, for Thee to drive out nations and dwellings from before Thy people, whom Thou didst redeem for Thyself from Egypt.
7:24Thou didst prepare Thy people Israel for Thyself as a people for ever, and Thou, Lord, becamest their God.
7:25Now, my Lord, Lord, confirm for ever the word Thou hast spoken concerning Thy servant and his house, Lord Almighty, God of Israel. And now, as Thou hast spoken,
7:26may Thy name be magnified for ever.
7:27Lord Almighty, God of Israel, Thou hast revealed to Thy servant’s ear, saying, ‘I will build you a house.’ Therefore Thy servant has found the heart to pray this prayer to Thee.
7:28Now, my Lord, Lord, Thou art God, and Thy words will be true. Thou hast spoken these good things concerning Thy servant.

7:29Now begin and bless Thy servant’s house, that it may remain before Thee for ever. For it is Thou, my Lord, Lord, who hast spoken, and through Thy blessing Thy servant’s house will be blessed for ever.”
8:1After this, David struck the foreigners and routed them. David took the separated territory from the foreigners’ hand.

8:2David struck Moab and measured them with cords, making them lie on the ground. Two measured lengths were for putting to death, and two measured lengths he kept alive. Moab became David’s servants, bringing gifts.
8:3David struck Hadadezer son of Raab, king of Zobah, as he went to establish his control at the River Euphrates.
8:4David captured one thousand of his chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David disabled all the chariots, but left a hundred chariots from them.
8:5Syria of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, and David struck down twenty-two thousand Syrian men.
8:6David placed a garrison in Syria around Damascus, and Syria became David’s servants, bringing gifts. The Lord gave David victory wherever he went.

8:7David took the gold armlets that were on the servants of Hadadezer king of Zobah and brought them to Jerusalem. Shishak king of Egypt took them when he went up to Jerusalem in the days of Rehoboam son of Solomon.
8:8From Masbak, from Hadadezer’s selected cities, King David took a great quantity of bronze. With it Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, the basins, and all the vessels.
8:9Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck all Hadadezer’s force,

8:10and Toi sent his son Ieddouran to King David to inquire about peace and bless him because he had fought Hadadezer and struck him, for he had been opposed to Hadadezer. In his hands were silver vessels, gold vessels, and bronze vessels.
8:11King David dedicated these to the Lord, with the silver and gold he had dedicated from all the cities he had dominated:
8:12from Idumea, Moab, the sons of Ammon, the foreigners, Amalek, and the spoil of Hadadezer son of Raab, king of Zobah.
8:13David made a name for himself. When he returned, he struck eighteen thousand in Idumea at Gaimale.
8:14He placed a garrison in Idumea, throughout all Idumea, and all the Idumeans became the king’s servants. The Lord gave David victory wherever he went.
8:15David reigned over Israel, and David administered judgment and righteousness for all his people.
8:16Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahia was over the records;
8:17Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Asa was the scribe;
8:18and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was counselor, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were palace officials.
9:1David said, “Is anyone still left of Saul’s house, that I may show him mercy for Jonathan’s sake?”
9:2There was a servant from Saul’s house named Ziba, and they called him to David. The king said to him, “Are you Ziba?” He said, “I am your servant.”
9:3The king said, “Is there still a man left of Saul’s house, that I may show him God’s mercy?” Ziba said to the king, “Jonathan still has a son whose feet have been injured.”
9:4The king said, “Where is he?” Ziba said to the king, “Behold, in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, of Lo-debar.”
9:5King David sent and brought him from the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
9:6Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, came to King David, fell on his face, and bowed down to him. David said to him, “Mephibosheth!” He said, “Here is your servant.”

9:7David said to him, “Do not fear. I will certainly show you mercy because of Jonathan your father. I will restore to you all the land of Saul your father’s father, and you will eat bread at my table continually.”
9:8Mephibosheth bowed down and said, “Who am I, your servant, that you have looked toward a dead dog like me?”
9:9The king called Ziba, Saul’s attendant, and said to him, “Everything that belongs to Saul and his whole house I have given to your master’s son.

9:10You, your sons, and your servants shall work the land for him. You shall bring loaves to your master’s son, and he will eat them. But Mephibosheth, your master’s son, shall eat bread continually at my table.” Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
9:11Ziba said to the king, “Your servant will do according to everything my lord the king has commanded his servant.” Mephibosheth ate at David’s table like one of the king’s sons.
9:12Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica. The whole household of Ziba were Mephibosheth’s servants.
9:13Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the king’s table. He was lame in both his feet.
10:1After this, the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son became king in his place.

10:2David said, “I will show mercy to Hanun son of Nahash, as his father showed mercy to me.” David sent his servants to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants entered the land of the sons of Ammon.

10:3The leaders of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, “Do you think David is glorifying your father by sending comforters to you? Has David not sent his servants to you so that they may search the city, spy it out, and inspect it?”
10:4Hanun took David’s servants, shaved their beards, cut their cloaks in half at their hips, and sent them away.
10:5David was told about the men, and he sent to meet them, for the men had been greatly dishonoured. The king said, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow, and then you shall return.”

10:6The sons of Ammon saw that David’s people had been put to shame. They sent and hired Syria of Beth-rehob, twenty thousand foot soldiers, the king of Maacah, a thousand men, and Istob, twelve thousand men.
10:7David heard and sent Joab and the whole force, the mighty men.
10:8The sons of Ammon came out and drew up for battle at the gate’s entrance. Syria of Zobah and Rehob, Istob, and Maacah were by themselves in the field.
10:9Joab saw that the battle faced him from the front and from behind. He selected some of all Israel’s young men, and they drew up against Syria.
10:10He placed the rest of the people in the hand of Abishai his brother, and they drew up against the sons of Ammon.
10:11He said, “If Syria is too strong for me, you all shall come to my rescue. If the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, we will be there to rescue you.
10:12Be courageous, and let us show strength for our people and for the cities of our God. The Lord will do what is good in His eyes.”
10:13Joab and his people with him advanced to battle against Syria, and they fled before him.
10:14The sons of Ammon saw that Syria had fled, and they fled before Abishai and entered the city. Joab returned from the sons of Ammon, and they came to Jerusalem.
10:15Syria saw that it had been defeated before Israel, and they gathered together.
10:16Hadadezer sent and gathered Syria from beyond the River Chalamak. They came to Ailam, with Shobach, leader of Hadadezer’s force, at their head.
10:17David was told. He gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan, and they came to Ailam. Syria drew up opposite David and fought with him.
10:18Syria fled before Israel. David destroyed seven hundred Syrian chariots and killed forty thousand horsemen. He struck Shobach, the leader of his force, and he died there.
10:19All the kings serving Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated before Israel. They deserted to Israel and served them, and Syria feared to help the sons of Ammon again.

11:1At the return of the year, at the time of the kings’ expedition, David sent Joab, his servants with him, and all Israel. They devastated the sons of Ammon and laid siege to Rabbah, while David remained in Jerusalem.
11:2Toward evening David rose from his bed and walked on the roof of the king’s house. From the roof he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was very beautiful in appearance.
11:3David sent and sought the woman. It was said, “Is this not Bathsheba daughter of Eliab, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?”
11:4David sent messengers and took her. She came to him, and he lay with her. She was purifying herself from her impurity, and she returned to her house.
11:5The woman conceived. She sent word and reported to David, saying, “I am pregnant.”
11:6David sent to Joab, saying, “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” Joab sent Uriah to David.
11:7Uriah arrived and came in to him, and David asked about Joab’s welfare, the people’s welfare, and the welfare of the war.
11:8David said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” Uriah left the king’s house, and a portion from the king went out after him.
11:9Uriah lay down by the king’s door with his lord’s servants, and did not go down to his house.
11:10David was told, “Uriah did not go down to his house.” David said to Uriah, “Have you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?”

11:11Uriah said to David, “The ark, Israel, and Judah are staying in tents. My lord Joab and my lord’s servants are camping in the open field. Shall I go to my house to eat, drink, and lie with my wife? How could I? As your soul lives, I will not do this thing.”
11:12David said to Uriah, “Stay here today also, and tomorrow I will send you away.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next.
11:13David called him, and he ate and drank before him, and David made him drunk. In the evening he went out to lie on his bed with his lord’s servants, but he did not go down to his house.
11:14In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by Uriah’s hand.
11:15He wrote in the letter, “Bring Uriah to face the fiercest battle, and you shall withdraw from behind him, and he will be struck and die.”
11:16As Joab kept watch over the city, he placed Uriah where he knew there were powerful men.
11:17The city’s men came out and fought Joab. Some of the people, David’s servants, fell, and Uriah the Hittite also died.
11:18Joab sent and reported to the king all the matters of the battle,
11:19and instructed the messenger, “When you have finished telling the king all the matters of the battle,
11:20if the king’s anger rises and he says to you, ‘Why did you go so near the city to fight? Did you not know they would shoot arrows from above the wall?

11:21Who struck Abimelech son of Jerubbaal? Did not a woman throw a fragment of a millstone on him from above the wall, so that he died at Thamasi? Why did you go so near the wall?’ Then say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite also died.’”

11:22Joab’s messenger went to the king in Jerusalem, arrived, and reported to David everything Joab had told him, all the matters of the battle. David became angry with Joab and said to the messenger, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Did you not know you would be struck from the wall? Who struck Abimelech son of Jerubbaal? Did not a woman throw a fragment of a millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Thamasi? Why did you go so near the wall?”
11:23The messenger said to David, “The men grew strong against us and came out against us in the field. We pressed them as far as the gate’s entrance,
11:24and the archers shot at your servants from above the wall. Some of the king’s servants died, and your servant Uriah the Hittite also died.”

11:25David said to the messenger, “Tell Joab this: ‘Do not regard this matter as evil, for the sword devours sometimes this way and sometimes that way. Strengthen your battle against the city and pull it down.’ And encourage him.”
11:26Uriah’s wife heard that Uriah her husband had died, and she beat herself in mourning for her husband.
11:27When the mourning passed, David sent and brought her into his house. She became his wife and bore him a son. But what David had done appeared evil in the Lord’s eyes.
12:1The Lord sent Nathan the prophet to David. He came in to him and said, “There were two men in one city, one rich and the other poor.
12:2The rich man had very many flocks and herds.

12:3The poor man had nothing except one little ewe lamb that he had acquired, preserved, and reared. It grew up with him and his sons together. It ate from his bread, drank from his cup, and slept in his bosom. It was like a daughter to him.

12:4A passerby came to the rich man. He was unwilling to take from his own flocks or herds to prepare a meal for the traveling stranger who had come to him. He took the poor man’s ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”
12:5David became intensely angry with the man. David said to Nathan, “As the Lord lives, the man who did this deserves death!
12:6He must repay the ewe lamb sevenfold, because he did this thing and had no pity.”
12:7Nathan said to David, “You are the man who did this! Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: ‘I am the One who anointed you king over Israel, and I am the One who rescued you from Saul’s hand.
12:8I gave you your lord’s house and your lord’s wives into your bosom. I gave you the house of Israel and Judah. If this is little, I will add more like these things.

12:9Why have you treated the Lord’s word as worthless by doing evil in His eyes? You struck Uriah the Hittite with the sword and took his wife to be your wife; him you killed with the sword of the sons of Ammon.
12:10Now the sword will never depart from your house, because you held Me in contempt and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.’

12:11Thus says the Lord: ‘Behold, I am raising up calamities against you from your own house. I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbour, and he will lie with your wives before this sun.
12:12You acted in secret, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before this sun.’”
12:13David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the Lord.” Nathan said to David, “The Lord also has put away your sin; you will certainly not die.
12:14Nevertheless, because by this deed you have thoroughly provoked the Lord’s enemies, your son who was born to you will certainly die.”
12:15Nathan went to his house. The Lord struck down the child whom Uriah’s wife had borne to David, and he became ill.
12:16David sought God concerning the child. David fasted, went in, and spent the night in sackcloth on the ground.
12:17The elders of his house stood beside him to raise him from the ground, but he refused and would not eat bread with them.

12:18On the seventh day the child died. David’s servants were afraid to tell him that the child had died, for they said, “While the child was still alive, we spoke to him and he did not listen to us. How can we tell him that the child has died? He may do harmful things.”
12:19David understood that his servants were whispering and perceived that the child had died. David said to his servants, “Has the child died?” They said, “He has died.”

12:20David rose from the ground, washed, anointed himself, and changed his clothes. He entered God’s house and bowed down to Him. Then he entered his own house and asked for bread to eat; they set bread before him, and he ate.
12:21His servants said to him, “What is this that you have done? While the child was still alive, you fasted and wept and kept vigil, but when the child died, you rose and ate bread and drank.”
12:22David said, “While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept, because I said, ‘Who knows whether the Lord will have mercy on me and the child will live?’
12:23But now he has died. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.”
12:24David comforted Bathsheba his wife. He went in to her and lay with her. She conceived, bore a son, and named him Solomon. The Lord loved him.
12:25He sent word through Nathan the prophet, and he called the child Idedi because of the Lord.
12:26Joab fought at Rabbah of the sons of Ammon and captured the royal city.
12:27Joab sent messengers to David and said, “I have fought at Rabbah and captured the city of waters.
12:28Now gather the rest of the people, encamp against the city, and take it first, lest I take the city first and my name be called over it.”
12:29David gathered all the people, went to Rabbah, fought there, and captured it.

12:30He took the crown of Melchol their king from his head. Its weight was a talent of gold and precious stone, and it was placed on David’s head. He brought out a very great quantity of spoil from the city.

12:31He brought out the people who were in it and put them to the saw and the iron threshing implements, and led them through the brickworks. He did this to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
13:1After this, Absalom son of David had a sister very beautiful in appearance, named Tamar, and Amnon son of David loved her.
13:2Amnon was so distressed over Tamar his sister that he became ill. She was a virgin, and it seemed exceedingly difficult to Amnon to do anything to her.
13:3Amnon had a companion named Jonadab son of Shimeah, David’s brother. Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
13:4He said to him, “Why are you so weak morning after morning, king’s son? Will you not tell me?” Amnon said to him, “I love Tamar, the sister of Absalom my brother.”

13:5Jonadab said to him, “Lie down on your bed and act ill. Your father will come in to see you. Say to him, ‘Please let Tamar my sister come and feed me. Let her prepare food before my eyes so that I can watch and eat from her hands.’”

13:6Amnon lay down and became ill. The king came in to see him. Amnon said to the king, “Please let Tamar my sister come to me and make two little loaves before my eyes, and I will eat from her hand.”
13:7David sent word to Tamar at the house: “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare food for him.”
13:8Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, who was lying down. She took the dough, mixed it, made little loaves before his eyes, and cooked the little loaves.
13:9She took the frying pan and emptied it before him, but he refused to eat. Amnon said, “Take every man away from me.” They took every man away from him.
13:10Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the inner room, and I will eat from your hand.” Tamar took the little loaves she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother in the bedroom,
13:11and brought the food near for him to eat. He seized her and said to her, “Come, lie with me, my sister.”
13:12She said to him, “No, my brother! Do not violate me! Such a thing must not be done in Israel. Do not commit this folly!
13:13Where could I carry my disgrace? And you would become like one of the foolish men in Israel. Please speak to the king now, for he certainly will not withhold me from you.”
13:14Amnon refused to listen to her. He overpowered her, violated her, and lay with her.
13:15Then Amnon hated her with very great hatred. The hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. Amnon said to her, “Arise and go!”
13:16Tamar said to him, “No, brother! This last evil, sending me away, is greater than the first thing you have done to me.” But Amnon refused to listen to her.
13:17He called his young servant who was in charge of his house and said to him, “Send this one away from me, outside, and lock the door behind her.”

13:18She was wearing a tunic with sleeves reaching the wrists, for this was how the king’s virgin daughters wore their outer garments. His attendant brought her outside and locked the door behind her.
13:19Tamar took ashes and put them on her head and tore the tunic with sleeves reaching the wrists that she was wearing. She put her hands on her head and went away, crying out as she went.

13:20Absalom her brother said to her, “Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now, my sister, be silent, for he is your brother. Do not set your heart on speaking about this matter.” Tamar lived as a widow in the house of Absalom her brother.
13:21King David heard all these things and became very angry. But he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, since he was his firstborn.
13:22Absalom spoke to Amnon neither evil nor good, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had violated Tamar his sister.
13:23After two full years, Absalom had sheep shearers at Baal-hazor, adjoining Ephraim. Absalom invited all the king’s sons.
13:24Absalom came to the king and said, “They are shearing sheep for your servant. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant.”
13:25The king said to Absalom, “No, my son. Please do not let us all go, so that we do not burden you.” Absalom pressed him, but he refused to go and blessed him.
13:26Absalom said, “If not, please let Amnon my brother go with us.” The king said to him, “Why should he go with you?”
13:27Absalom pressed him, and he sent Amnon and all the king’s sons with him. Absalom prepared a drinking feast like the king’s drinking feast.

13:28Absalom instructed his young men, “Watch when Amnon’s heart is merry with wine. When I say to you, ‘Strike Amnon,’ kill him. Do not be afraid. Am I not the one commanding you? Be courageous and be powerful men.”
13:29Absalom’s young men did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded them. All the king’s sons rose, each mounted his mule, and they fled.
13:30While they were on the way, a report came to David: “Absalom has struck all the king’s sons; not even one of them is left.”
13:31The king rose, tore his clothes, and lay on the ground. All his servants standing around him tore their clothes.

13:32Jonadab son of Shimeah, David’s brother, answered, “Let my lord the king not say that he has killed all the young men, the king’s sons. Amnon alone has died. He had been marked out by Absalom from the day he violated Tamar his sister.
13:33Now let my lord the king not take to heart the report that all the king’s sons have died. Only Amnon has died.”

13:34Absalom escaped. The young watchman raised his eyes and saw a large crowd coming along the road behind him, from the side of the mountain, on the descent. The watchman came and reported to the king, “I have seen men coming from the road of Horonen, from the side of the mountain.”
13:35Jonadab said to the king, “Behold, the king’s sons are here. It has happened just as your servant said.”
13:36As he finished speaking, the king’s sons arrived, raised their voices, and wept. The king and all his servants also wept very bitterly.
13:37Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, in the land of Machad. King David mourned for his son all those days.
13:38Absalom escaped and went to Geshur, and he was there three years.
13:39The king’s spirit ceased going out after Absalom, for he had been comforted concerning Amnon, since he was dead.
14:1Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the king’s heart was on Absalom.

14:2Joab sent to Tekoa and brought from there a wise woman. He said to her, “Please mourn. Put on mourning clothes and do not anoint yourself with oil. Be like a woman who has mourned someone dead for many days.
14:3Go to the king and speak to him in this manner.” Joab put the words into her mouth.
14:4The woman of Tekoa came in to the king, fell facedown to the ground, bowed down to him, and said, “Help, O king, help!”
14:5The king said to her, “What troubles you?” She said, “Indeed, I am a widow; my husband has died.
14:6Your servant had two sons. Both fought in the field, with no one between them to intervene. One struck his brother and killed him.

14:7Now the whole paternal family has risen against your servant. They say, ‘Hand over the one who struck his brother, and we will put him to death for the life of the brother he killed. We will remove your heir as well.’ They would extinguish my last remaining ember, leaving my husband neither remnant nor name on the face of the earth.”
14:8The king said, “Go to your house in good health, and I will give orders concerning you.”
14:9The woman of Tekoa said to the king, “Let the lawlessness fall on me, my lord the king, and on my father’s house; let the king and his throne be innocent.”
14:10The king said, “Who is speaking to you? Bring him to me, and he will not touch him again.”

14:11She said, “Please let the king remember the Lord his God, for a blood avenger to become great in destruction; and they will certainly not remove my son.” He said, “As the Lord lives, not a hair of your son will fall to the ground.”
14:12The woman said, “Please let your servant speak a word to my lord the king.” He said, “Speak.”
14:13The woman said, “Why have you planned such a thing against God’s people? Is this word from the king’s mouth not an offence, since the king does not bring back his own banished one?
14:14We must certainly die and are like water poured onto the ground that will not be gathered again. God will take a life, while planning to banish a banished one from Him.
14:15What I have come to say to my lord the king is this, because the people will see me. Your servant will say, ‘Let someone speak to the king; perhaps the king will grant his servant’s request,
14:16for the king will listen and deliver his servant from the hand of the man seeking to remove me and my son from God’s inheritance.’”
14:17The woman said, “May my lord the king’s word be an offering, for my lord the king is like God’s angel in hearing good and evil. The Lord your God will be with you.”
14:18The king answered the woman, “Please do not hide from me anything I ask you.” The woman said, “Please let my lord the king speak.”

14:19The king said, “Is Joab’s hand with you in all this?” The woman said to the king, “As your soul lives, my lord the king, there is no turning right or left from anything my lord the king has said. Your servant Joab commanded me; he put all these words into your servant’s mouth.
14:20Your servant Joab did this to turn the matter around. My lord is wise, with the wisdom of God’s angel, to know everything in the land.”
14:21The king said to Joab, “I have now acted for you according to this request of yours. Go and bring back the young man Absalom.”

14:22Joab fell facedown to the ground, bowed down, and blessed the king. Joab said, “Today your servant knows that I have found favour in your eyes, my lord the king, because my lord the king has granted his servant’s request.”
14:23Joab rose, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
14:24The king said, “Let him turn aside to his own house; he must not see my face.” Absalom turned aside to his own house and did not see the king’s face.
14:25In all Israel no man was so highly praised as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
14:26When he cut the hair of his head—from one period of days to another he cut it because it grew heavy on him—he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels by the royal shekel.
14:27Three sons and one daughter were born to Absalom. Her name was Tamar, and she was a very beautiful woman. She became the wife of Rehoboam son of Solomon and bore him Abijah.
14:28Absalom lived in Jerusalem two full years without seeing the king’s face.
14:29Absalom sent for Joab to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. He sent to him a second time, but Joab refused to appear.

14:30Absalom said to his servants, “Behold, Joab’s plot in the field is beside mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire.” Absalom’s servants burned the barley. Joab’s servants came to him with their clothes torn and said, “Absalom’s servants have set the plot on fire.”
14:31Joab rose, came to Absalom at his house, and said to him, “Why have your servants set my plot on fire?”

14:32Absalom said to Joab, “I sent to you, saying, ‘Come here, and I will send you to the king to say, “Why did I come from Geshur? It would be better for me still to be there.”’ Now behold, I have not seen the king’s face. If there is wrongdoing in me, put me to death.”
14:33Joab went in to the king and told him. The king summoned Absalom, who came to the king, bowed down to him, and fell facedown to the ground before him. The king kissed Absalom warmly.
15:1After this, Absalom provided himself with chariots, horses, and fifty men to run ahead of him.

15:2Absalom would rise early and stand beside the road to the gate. Whenever a man with a case came before the king for judgment, Absalom called to him, “What city are you from?” The man would answer, “Your servant is from one of Israel’s tribes.”
15:3Absalom would say to him, “Your claims are good and straightforward, but no one from the king is here to hear you.”
15:4Absalom would say, “Who will appoint me judge in the land, so that every man with a dispute or case will come to me and I will give him justice?”
15:5Whenever a man approached to bow down to him, Absalom would stretch out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him warmly.
15:6Absalom did this to all Israel who came to the king for judgment. Absalom made the hearts of the men of Israel his own.
15:7At the end of forty years, Absalom said to his father, “Please let me go to Hebron and fulfill the vows I made to the Lord.
15:8Your servant made a vow while I was living at Geshur in Syria: ‘If the Lord indeed brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the Lord.’”
15:9The king said to him, “Go in peace.” He rose and went to Hebron.
15:10Absalom sent spies throughout all Israel’s tribes, saying, “When you hear the horn’s sound, say, ‘King Absalom has begun to reign in Hebron!’”
15:11Two hundred invited men went with Absalom from Jerusalem. They went in their simplicity and knew nothing of the matter.
15:12While sacrificing, Absalom sent and summoned Ahithophel the Gelmonite, David’s counselor, from his city Gola. The conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.
15:13A messenger came to David, saying, “The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom.”

15:14David said to all his servants with him in Jerusalem, “Rise, let us flee, for we have no deliverance from Absalom. Hurry to leave, lest he hurry and overtake us, thrust calamity upon us, and strike the city with the sword’s edge.”
15:15The king’s servants said to the king, “Whatever our lord the king chooses—here are your servants.”
15:16The king went out, with all his household on foot. The king left ten of his concubines to guard the house.
15:17The king went out, with all his servants on foot, and they stopped at the house far away.

15:18All his servants passed beside him, with all the Chetti and all the Pelethites, and they stood at the olive tree in the wilderness. All the people passed close beside him, all those around him, all the strong men and all the warriors—six hundred men—and they were at his side. All the Cherethites, all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites—six hundred men who had come on foot from Gath—passed before the king.
15:19The king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you also go with us? Return and stay with the king, for you are a stranger and have migrated from your own place.

15:20If you arrived yesterday, shall I move you with us today, and must you also change your place? Yesterday was your departure; shall I move you with us today to go along? I myself will go wherever I may go. Return, and take your brothers back with you, and the Lord will show you mercy and truth.”
15:21Ittai answered the king, “As the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord may be, whether in death or in life, there your servant will be.”
15:22The king said to Ittai, “Come and cross over with me.” Ittai the Gittite passed on with all his servants and the whole crowd with him.
15:23All the land wept aloud. All the people passed through the Kidron torrent, and the king crossed the Kidron torrent. All the people and the king passed toward the road to the wilderness.

15:24Zadok was also there, with all the Levites carrying the ark of the Lord’s covenant from Baithar. They set down God’s ark, and Abiathar went up until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
15:25The king said to Zadok, “Take God’s ark back to the city. If I find favour in the Lord’s eyes, He will bring me back and show me the ark and its beauty.
15:26But if He says, ‘I have not taken pleasure in you,’ here I am. Let Him do to me what is good in His eyes.”
15:27The king said to Zadok the priest, “Behold, you are returning to the city in peace, with your two sons—Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan son of Abiathar—with you.
15:28Behold, I am encamped at Araboth in the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”
15:29Zadok and Abiathar took the ark back to Jerusalem, and it stayed there.
15:30David went up the ascent of the Olives, weeping as he went. His head was covered, and he walked barefoot. All the people with him covered their heads, each one, and went up weeping as they went.
15:31David was told, “Ahithophel too is among the conspirators with Absalom.” David said, “Lord my God, please scatter Ahithophel’s counsel.”
15:32As David came to Roos, where he bowed down to God, Hushai the Archite, David’s companion, came to meet him, his tunic torn and earth on his head.
15:33David said to him, “If you cross over with me, you will be a burden to me.

15:34But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, ‘Your brothers have passed on, and the king, your father, has passed on behind me. Now I am your servant, O king; let me live. I was your father’s servant then and just now, and now I am your servant,’ you can scatter Ahithophel’s counsel for me.
15:35Behold, Zadok and Abiathar the priests are there with you. Whatever you hear from the king’s house, tell Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
15:36Their two sons are there with them: Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, and Jonathan, Abiathar’s son. Send me through them everything you hear.”
15:37Hushai, David’s companion, entered the city, while Absalom was coming into Jerusalem.

16:1David had passed a little beyond Roos when Ziba, Mephibosheth’s servant, met him with a pair of loaded donkeys. On them were two hundred loaves, a hundred raisins, a hundred dates, and a vessel of wine.

16:2The king said to Ziba, “What are these for?” Ziba said, “The pack animals are for the king’s household to ride; the bread and dates are for the young men to eat; the wine is for those who grow faint in the wilderness to drink.”
16:3The king said, “Where is your lord’s son?” Ziba said to the king, “He is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, ‘Today the house of Israel will restore my father’s kingdom to me.’”
16:4The king said to Ziba, “Everything belonging to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba bowed down and said, “May I find favour in your eyes, my lord the king.”
16:5King David came to Bahurim. A man from the kin of Saul’s house was coming out from there, named Shimei son of Gera. He came out, continually cursing,
16:6throwing stones at David and all King David’s servants, while all the people and all the powerful men were at the king’s right and left.
16:7Shimei said as he cursed, “Get out, get out, man of bloodshed, lawless man!

16:8The Lord has brought back upon you all the blood of Saul’s house, because you became king in his place. The Lord has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son. Now you are in calamity, because you are a man of bloodshed.”
16:9Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? I will cross over and take off his head.”
16:10The king said, “What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Leave him alone, and let him curse this way, because the Lord has told him to curse David. Who can say, ‘Why have you done this?’”
16:11David said to Abishai and all his servants, “My own son, who came from my belly, seeks my life. And now this son of the Benjaminite as well! Leave him alone to curse, for the Lord has told him.
16:12Perhaps the Lord will look upon my humiliation and repay me with good things in place of his curse this day.”
16:13David and his men went along the road. Shimei went along the mountainside beside him, walking and cursing, throwing stones from his flank and showering dust.
16:14The king and all his people arrived exhausted, and they refreshed themselves there.
16:15Absalom and every man of Israel entered Jerusalem, with Ahithophel beside him.
16:16When Hushai the Archite, David’s companion, came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, “Long live the king!”
16:17Absalom said to Hushai, “Is this your mercy toward your companion? Why did you not depart with your companion?”
16:18Hushai said to Absalom, “No. From now on I will belong to the one whom the Lord, this people, and every man of Israel have chosen, and I will stay with him.
16:19And secondly, whom should I serve? Should I not serve in the presence of his son? As I served before your father, so I will be before you.”
16:20Absalom said to Ahithophel, “All of you, bring forward your counsel about what we should do.”

16:21Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Go in to your father’s concubines, whom he left to guard his house. All Israel will hear that you have disgraced your father, and the hands of everyone with you will be strengthened.”
16:22They pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to his father’s concubines before the eyes of all Israel.
16:23The counsel Ahithophel gave in former days was regarded as though one had inquired of God’s word. So was all Ahithophel’s counsel, both to David and to Absalom.
17:1Ahithophel said to Absalom, “I will choose twelve thousand men for myself. I will rise and pursue David by night.
17:2I will come upon him while he is weary and his hands are weak. I will throw him into confusion, and all the people with him will flee. I will strike down the king alone.
17:3I will bring all the people back to you, as a bride returns to her husband. You seek only one man’s life, and all the people will have peace.”
17:4The proposal was right in the eyes of Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
17:5Absalom said, “Call Hushai the Archite as well, so that we may hear what he too has to say.”
17:6Hushai entered before Absalom. Absalom said to him, “Ahithophel has spoken in this way. Should we act on his proposal? If not, you speak.”
17:7Hushai said to Absalom, “This counsel Ahithophel has given is not good this time.”

17:8Hushai continued, “You know your father and his men: they are very powerful, bitter in their souls, like a bear bereaved of her cubs in the field and like a fierce sow on the plain. Your father is a man of war; he will certainly not give the people lodging.

17:9Even now he is hiding in one of the hills or in some other place. When he falls upon them at the outset, whoever hears will say, ‘There has been a crushing defeat among the people following Absalom.’
17:10Even a valiant man whose heart is like a lion’s heart—his heart will utterly melt, for all Israel knows that your father is powerful and those with him are men of strength.
17:11This is the counsel I have given: all Israel will gather to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as numerous as the sand beside the sea, with you yourself going in their midst.
17:12We will come upon him in whatever place we find him, and encamp against him as dew falls on the ground. We will leave neither him nor even one of the men with him.
17:13If he withdraws into a city, all Israel will take ropes to that city. We will drag it down to the torrent so that not even a stone is left there.”

17:14Absalom and every man of Israel said, “Hushai the Archite’s counsel is better than Ahithophel’s.” The Lord had commanded that Ahithophel’s good counsel be scattered, so that the Lord might bring all these calamities upon Absalom.
17:15Hushai the Archite said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, “Ahithophel advised Absalom and the elders of Israel in such and such a way, and I advised them in such and such a way.
17:16Now send quickly and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night in Araboth of the wilderness. Hurry across, lest it swallow up the king and all the people with him.’”
17:17Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at the spring of Rogel. The handmaid went and informed them, and they went and reported to King David, for they could not be seen entering the city.
17:18A young man saw them and told Absalom. The two hurried away and entered a man’s house in Bahurim. He had a pit in his courtyard, and they went down into it.
17:19The woman took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the pit. She cooled grain on it, and nothing was discovered.

17:20Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house and asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman said to them, “They have gone a little beyond the water.” They searched but did not find them, and returned to Jerusalem.

17:21After they left, the two came up from the pit, went to King David, and reported to him. They said to David, “Rise and cross the water quickly, for this is what Ahithophel advised concerning you.”
17:22David and all the people with him rose and crossed the Jordan. By morning light not one who had not crossed the Jordan had escaped notice.

17:23Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been carried out. He saddled his donkey, rose, and went home to his city. He gave instructions to his household, hanged himself, and died. He was buried in his father’s tomb.
17:24David passed on to Mahanaim. Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and every man of Israel with him.
17:25Absalom appointed Amasa over the army in Joab’s place. Amasa was the son of a man named Jethro the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.
17:26All Israel and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
17:27When David came to Mahanaim, Ouesbi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim
17:28brought ten beds, rugs with pile on both sides, ten cauldrons, pottery vessels, wheat, barley, flour, barley meal, beans, and lentils,
17:29also honey, butter, sheep, and cheese from cattle. They brought these for David and the people with him to eat, for they said, “The people are hungry, exhausted, and thirsty in the wilderness.”
18:1David mustered the people with him and appointed commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds over them.

18:2David sent out the people: one third under Joab, one third under Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and one third under Ittai the Gittite. David said to the people, “I too will certainly go out with you.”

18:3They said, “You must not go out. If we flee, they will pay no attention to us; if half of us die, they will pay no attention to us. You are worth ten thousand of us. It is better now for you to be a help to us in the city.”
18:4The king said to them, “I will do whatever pleases you.” The king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and thousands.
18:5The king commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “For my sake, spare the young man Absalom.” All the people heard the king command all the officers concerning Absalom.
18:6All the people went out into the forest to face Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
18:7The people of Israel fell there before David’s servants. The crushing defeat that day was great: twenty thousand men.
18:8The battle spread there across the whole land, and the forest devoured more of the people that day than the sword devoured among them.

18:9Absalom encountered David’s servants. Absalom was riding his mule, and the mule went under the thick growth of the great oak. His head hung in the oak, and he hung between heaven and earth, while the mule beneath him went on.
18:10A man saw it and told Joab, “I have just seen Absalom hanging in the oak.”
18:11Joab said to the man reporting to him, “You saw him! Why did you not strike him to the ground? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a belt.”

18:12The man said to Joab, “Even if I weigh a thousand silver shekels in my hands, I will certainly not put out my hand against the king’s son. In our hearing the king commanded you, Abishai, and Ittai, ‘Guard the young man Absalom for me,
18:13so as to do no wrong against his life.’ Nothing will escape the king’s notice, and you yourself would stand opposite me.”

18:14Joab said, “I will begin this myself; I will not wait before you like this.” Joab took three darts in his hand and drove them into Absalom’s heart. While he was still alive in the heart of the oak,
18:15ten young men who carried Joab’s armour surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.
18:16Joab sounded the horn, and the people turned back from pursuing Israel, for Joab spared the people.
18:17He took Absalom and threw him into a great chasm in the forest, into the great pit, and raised a very large heap of stones over him. All Israel fled, each to his tent.

18:18While still alive, Absalom set up for himself the pillar in which he was taken, and erected it to take—the pillar in the King’s Valley—for he said that he had no son to keep his name in remembrance. He called the pillar Absalom’s Hand, to this day.
18:19Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Let me run and bring the king good news: the Lord has vindicated him against the hand of his enemies.”
18:20Joab said to him, “You are not the man to bring good news today. You may bring good news another day, but today you must not bring good news, because the king’s son is dead.”
18:21Joab said to Cushi, “Go, report to the king everything you have seen.” Cushi bowed to Joab and went out.
18:22Ahimaaz son of Zadok spoke again to Joab: “Let me too run after Cushi.” Joab said, “Why are you running, my son? Come here. There is no news that will benefit you by going.”
18:23He said, “What if I do run?” Joab told him, “Run.” Ahimaaz ran by the road of Kechar and overtook Cushi.
18:24David was sitting between the two gates. The watchman went up to the gate roof by the wall, raised his eyes, and saw a man running alone before him.
18:25The watchman called out and told the king. The king said, “If he is alone, there is good news in his mouth.” The man kept coming nearer.
18:26The watchman saw another man running. He called out by the gate, “There is another man running alone.” The king said, “He too brings good news.”
18:27The watchman said, “I recognize the first man’s running: it is like Ahimaaz son of Zadok’s.” The king said, “He is a good man; he comes with good news.”

18:28Ahimaaz called to the king, “Peace!” He bowed to the king with his face to the ground and said, “Blessed is the Lord your God, who has shut out the men who hated their hand against my lord the king.”
18:29The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom well?” Ahimaaz said, “I saw a great crowd when Joab sent the king’s servant and your servant, but I did not know what was there.”
18:30The king said, “Turn aside and stand here.” He turned aside and stood.
18:31Then Cushi arrived and said to the king, “Let my lord the king receive good news: the Lord has vindicated you today against the hand of all who rose against you.”
18:32The king asked Cushi, “Is the young man Absalom well?” Cushi said, “May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rose against him to do harm, be like that young man.”

19:1The king was shaken and went up to the upper chamber over the gate and wept. As he went, he said, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only my death had been granted instead of yours—I instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
19:2Joab was told, “The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.”
19:3That day’s deliverance turned to mourning for all the people, because the people heard that day, “The king is grieving over his son.”
19:4That day the people slipped into the city as people slip away in shame when they flee in battle.
19:5The king hid his face and cried aloud, “My son Absalom! Absalom, my son!”
19:6Joab came to the king in the house and said, “Today you have shamed all your servants, who rescued you today and the lives of your sons, daughters, wives, and concubines,

19:7by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you. Today you have declared that your officers and servants do not exist. I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us dead today, that would be right in your eyes.

19:8Now rise, go out, and speak to your servants’ hearts. I swear by the Lord: if you do not go out today, not one man will stay with you tonight. Understand this for yourself: this will be worse for you than all the calamity that has come upon you from your youth until now.”
19:9The king rose and sat in the gate. All the people announced, “The king is sitting in the gate,” and all the people came before the king. Israel had fled, each to his tents.

19:10All the people were disputing throughout all the tribes of Israel: “King David delivered us from all our enemies and rescued us from the hand of the foreigners. Now he has fled from the land and from his kingdom because of Absalom.
19:11Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. Why are you silent now about bringing the king back?” The word of all Israel reached the king.

19:12King David sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests: “Speak to the elders of Judah: ‘Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house? The word of all Israel has reached the king.
19:13You are my brothers, my bones and my flesh. Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house?’
19:14Say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my bone and my flesh? Now may God do so to me, and more besides, if you are not commander of the army before me always in Joab’s place.’”
19:15He turned the heart of every man of Judah as one man, and they sent word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.”
19:16The king returned and came as far as the Jordan. The men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and bring the king across the Jordan.
19:17Shimei son of Gera, son of the Benjaminite, from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David,

19:18with a thousand men from Benjamin beside him. Ziba, the servant of Saul’s house, was there, with his fifteen sons beside him and his twenty servants beside him. They made the Jordan ready before the king,

19:19and performed the service of bringing the king across. The ferry crossed to rouse the king’s household and do what was right in his eyes. Shimei son of Gera fell on his face before the king as he was crossing the Jordan.
19:20He said to the king, “Let my lord not reckon lawlessness. Do not remember your servant’s wrongs on the day my lord the king was leaving Jerusalem, so that the king takes them to heart.
19:21Your servant knows that I have sinned. See, I have come today ahead of all the house of Joseph, to come down and meet my lord the king.”
19:22Abishai son of Zeruiah answered, “Should Shimei not be put to death for this, since he cursed the Lord’s anointed?”

19:23David said, “What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah, that you should become a plotter against me today? No man of Israel will be put to death today, for I do not know whether I reign over Israel today.”
19:24The king said to Shimei, “You will certainly not die.” The king swore to him.

19:25Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul came down to meet the king. He had not tended his feet, cut his nails, trimmed his mustache, or washed his clothes from the day the king departed until the day he returned in peace.
19:26When he entered Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, “Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?”

19:27Mephibosheth said to him, “My lord the king, my servant deceived me. Your servant had said to him, ‘Saddle the donkey for me, so that I may ride it and go with the king,’ for your servant is lame.
19:28He schemed against your servant before my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of God; do what is good in your eyes.

19:29All my father’s house were nothing but men liable to death before my lord the king, yet you placed your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right have I to cry out again to the king?”
19:30The king said to him, “Why speak any further about your affairs? I have said: you and Ziba shall divide the land.”
19:31Mephibosheth said to the king, “Let him take it all, now that my lord the king has returned to his house in peace.”
19:32Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and crossed the Jordan with the king to escort him over the Jordan.
19:33Barzillai was a very old man, eighty years of age. He had supported the king during his stay at Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.
19:34The king said to Barzillai, “Cross over with me, and I will support your old age beside me in Jerusalem.”
19:35Barzillai said to the king, “How many days remain in the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

19:36I am eighty years old today. Can I discern good from bad? Can your servant still taste what I eat or drink? Can I still hear the voices of male and female singers? Why should your servant be a further burden to my lord the king?
19:37Your servant will cross the Jordan with the king only a little way. Why should the king repay me with this repayment?

19:38Please let your servant remain, so that I may die in my own city beside my father’s and mother’s grave. Here is your servant Chimham; he will cross with my lord the king. Do for him what is good in your eyes.”
19:39The king said, “Let Chimham cross with me, and I will do for him what is good in your eyes. Whatever you choose to ask of me, I will do for you.”
19:40All the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed. The king warmly kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned to his own place.
